To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the spatially averaged Hubble parameter is a function of the spatial average of the energy density and the averaged shear scalar, (2) the averaged energy density and shear scalar are functions of the spatial average over the energy density, the shear scalar, and the anisotropic stress.

1. the spatially averaged energy density is not equal to the average energy density in any fixed gauge; 2. the spatially average energy density is equal to the average of the energy density in the uniform curvature gauge; 3. the spatially-averaged energy density is equal (in the case of a scalar field with a quadratic potential) to the average energy in the uniform curvature and conformally Newtonian gauge;

the spatial average of the Einstein equations in a perturbed FLRW universe is not a closed set of equations, and that the corrections in the uniform curvature gauge are of the form of the Newtonian potential and are of order the square of the Newtonian perturbation, whereas in the conformal Newtonian gauge they are of order the Newtonian perturbations.
